skill.name: brenda-database
skill.description: Query the BRENDA enzyme database through its SOAP API, parse enzyme records, compare kinetic parameters, and generate analysis outputs for biochemical research.
skill.summary: Query BRENDA enzyme kinetics, reactions, organisms, and pathway data.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: AI review found no prompt injection, exfiltration intent, or obfuscated executable payload. Most alerts are false positives from EC numbers, Markdown fences, documentation, and normal imports. The confirmed issue is local export and report writing to caller-provided filenames.

remediation.suggestion: Validate filenames, restrict writes to an output directory, and reject path traversal or absolute paths by default.
Document that BRENDA credentials are only for official API authentication and should never be committed.
Label EC numbers and code fences clearly so automated review does not confuse them with IPs or shell execution.

- `get_modeling_parameters(ec_number, substrate)`: Get parameters for kinetic modeling
- `export_kinetic_data(ec_number, format, filename)`: Export data to file
- Verify BRENDA_EMAIL and BRENDA_PASSWORD in .env file

content.value_statement: Enzyme researchers need reliable access to kinetic parameters, reactions, organisms, and environmental conditions. This skill guides BRENDA SOAP API queries, parsing, comparison, visualization, and pathway analysis.
actual_capabilities: Retrieves BRENDA Km values, reactions, organism records, and substrate-specific enzyme data through documented SOAP queries.
Parses BRENDA response strings into structured enzyme, substrate, reaction, pH, and temperature fields.
Compares enzyme properties across organisms and substrates for candidate selection.
Analyzes cofactors, inhibitors, activators, environmental parameters, and substrate specificity.
Generates kinetic plots, organism comparisons, pH profiles, temperature profiles, and summary visualizations.
Builds pathway and retrosynthesis reports using enzyme availability and feasibility helpers.
limitations: Requires a BRENDA account, valid credentials, and network access to the BRENDA SOAP service.
Depends on external Python packages such as zeep, pandas, matplotlib, seaborn, and networkx.
BRENDA records can be incomplete, inconsistent, or unavailable for specific enzymes or organisms.
Export and report helpers can write local files when a filename is provided.

use_cases.title: Screen enzyme candidates
use_cases.description: Compare Km values, organisms, substrates, and reaction data before selecting enzymes for experiments.

use_cases.title: Plan metabolic pathways
use_cases.description: Find enzyme-supported routes to target products and summarize pathway feasibility with BRENDA evidence.

use_cases.title: Prepare teaching datasets
use_cases.description: Create clear summaries and plots of enzyme kinetics, pH profiles, and temperature behavior for instruction.

prompt_templates.title: Find enzyme data
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the BRENDA database skill to find Km values and reactions for EC [EC_NUMBER]. Summarize organisms, substrates, units, and missing fields.

prompt_templates.title: Compare organisms
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare EC [EC_NUMBER] across [ORGANISM_LIST]. Focus on Km, optimal pH, temperature, substrate, and data quality.

prompt_templates.title: Evaluate enzyme engineering options
prompt_templates.prompt: Find thermophilic or pH-stable variants for EC [EC_NUMBER]. Rank candidates by conditions, kinetic evidence, and practical limitations.

prompt_templates.title: Build a pathway report
prompt_templates.prompt: Use BRENDA pathway helpers to explore routes to [TARGET_PRODUCT]. Include enzymes, organisms, reactions, feasibility concerns, and recommended follow-up searches.

output_examples.input: Compare alcohol dehydrogenase across Escherichia coli, Saccharomyces cerevisiae, and Homo sapiens.
output_examples.output: A ranked comparison of organisms, available Km records, common substrates, optimal conditions, and gaps that need manual review.

output_examples.input: Find enzymes that can produce lactate and assess a short pathway.
output_examples.output: A pathway summary with candidate reactions, EC numbers, organism sources, enzyme availability, and feasibility warnings.

output_examples.input: Create a kinetic modeling summary for EC 1.1.1.1 with ethanol as substrate.
output_examples.output: A concise table-style narrative covering Km, Vmax, kcat availability, pH, temperature, and suggested plots.

best_practices: Use specific EC numbers, organisms, and substrates before broad wildcard searches.
Keep BRENDA credentials out of shared files and rotate them if exposed.
Validate parsed values against the source record before using them in models.
anti_patterns: Do not treat every BRENDA response as complete or experimentally comparable.
Do not run broad wildcard searches repeatedly without rate limits or caching.
Do not export reports to sensitive paths or shared folders without review.

faq.question: Does this skill require a BRENDA account?
faq.answer: Yes. BRENDA SOAP API access requires registered credentials.

faq.question: Can it retrieve Km and kcat values?
faq.answer: It focuses on Km data and includes helpers for modeling parameters when records are available.

faq.question: Can it compare enzymes across organisms?
faq.answer: Yes. The scripts include organism comparison helpers for kinetic and environmental properties.

faq.question: Does it create charts?
faq.answer: Yes. Visualization helpers generate kinetic, organism, pH, temperature, and substrate specificity plots.

faq.question: Does it work offline?
faq.answer: No. Live BRENDA queries require network access unless prior results were cached outside the skill.

faq.question: Is the data ready for publication?
faq.answer: No. Treat outputs as research aids and verify important values against BRENDA and primary literature.
